newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: THREE BROKERS CUT,TWO RAISE HOOGOVENS
newsitem.headline: THREE BROKERS CUT,TWO RAISE HOOGOVENS

text.p: Three brokers downgraded their recommendations on Dutch steel and aluminium group Hoogovens on Friday while two brokers upgraded their earnings per share (EPS) forecasts.
ABN Amro Hoare Govett analyst Henri Jongschaap cut his recommendation to Hold from Buy and adjusted his EPS numbers to reflect the conversion of a 300 million guilder bond.
His new EPS numbers are 12.25 guilders for 1997, down from 13.15, and 15.10 in 1998, down from 17.27.
He said the good outlook was fairly discounted in the share price and the shares should perform in line with the market.
Van Lanschot analyst Patrick Rutten downgraded his recommendation to Marketperformance from Marketoutperformance.
He said the economic outlook worldwide was improving and he expected aluminium and steel prices to rise in the second half of 1997 and into 1998.
But the share price, which closed on Thursday at 131.10 guilders, was at all time highs and he felt it could rise further only if the market was certain about 1999 earnings.
Effectenbank Stroeve changed its rating to Trading Underperformer from Outperformer and advised investors to buy the shares only if they dipped to 110.00 guilders.

But CS First Boston analyst Jeremy Fletcher upgraded his EPS forecasts for 1997 to 11.70 guilders, from 10.70, and for 1998 to 15.40 from 14.20, and raised his 12 month price target to 180 guilders from 115.

"These changes reflect margin improvements already achieved, additional cost cutting of 150 million guilders by the end of 1998 and the more certain outlook for price rises in 1998," he said in a research note.
ING Barings raised its EPS estimates to 12.20 guilders from 11.70 for 1997 and to 16.55 from 15.90 for 1998.
The firm said volumes in steel were picking up more strongly than expected, the product mix improved in the first half of 1997 and should turn out better in the second half.
It also said the effects of the high dollar and sterling would be even more positive than it had foreseen previously.
